The real issue? Bloated bureaucracy, not public health. The GAO’s own reports show HHS programs are riddled with inefficiency—like $141 billion in Medicare overpayments flagged for reform. Cutting bureaucratic bloat redirects resources to frontline care, not "slashing" it. 

When agencies balloon with middlemen instead of doctors, taxpayers lose. Streamlining 20K non-essential roles forces HHS to prioritize actual health outcomes over administrative waste. 

Accountability isn’t an attack—it’s how we save lives and stop fraud.
